title: The Unique Games Conjecture
aliases: hardness of almost satisfiable permutation constraints
decision_reason: Exact source formulation, independent specialist corroboration, baseline duplicate screening, current resolution searches and a separated adversarial draft review support admission as an open problem. No matching later resolution located as of September 17, 2026.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Finite bipartite graph with a permutation [r]->[r] on each edge
problem_fingerprint.dimension: Unbounded instance size, fixed r for each epsilon
problem_fingerprint.domain: All finite nonempty-edge bipartite unique-game instances
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Every epsilon in (0,1/2); exists r depending only on epsilon
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For each epsilon, one fixed alphabet yields NP-hardness of the promise distinction
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Number of satisfied edges divided by total number of edges, counting multiplicity if present
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Fix epsilon and r before instance size varies
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: NP-hardness of distinguishing value >=1-epsilon from value <=epsilon
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Classical NP-hardness; no entanglement; no P!=NP assumption needed to state hardness

statement_source_and_scope_match: FMW Conjecture 1.4 states the symmetric-gap version exactly. KRT Conjecture 1.2 states the equivalent two-error-parameter version; take both errors epsilon, or their minimum for the reverse implication.
proposed_statement_text: For every epsilon in (0,1/2), does some fixed alphabet size r make it NP-hard to distinguish bipartite unique games of classical value at least 1-epsilon from those of value at most epsilon? Each edge carries a permutation of [r], and value is the largest fraction of simultaneously satisfied edge constraints.
applied_significance: Would establish limits on polynomial-time approximation of finite optimization problems. HEILMAN26 Theorem 1.4 gives a current concrete conditional sharp MAX-3-CUT hardness consequence.

open_status_evidence_summary: FMW still explicitly formulates UGC as Conjecture 1.4 on September 14, 2026. Independent KRT gives the classical formulation and HEILMAN26 uses it as an assumption.
independent_status_corroboration: KRT and HEILMAN26 have no authors in common with FMW; the latter is a contemporary conditional application, not an independent proof of the conjecture.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: FMW explains the existing (1/2,epsilon) unique-game hardness and proves perfect-completeness hardness for 4-to-1 games. Neither supplies almost-one completeness for permutation constraints.
